text.p: An powerful earthquake rocked a mountainous area in northern Colombia on Tuesday but no deaths, injuries or serious damage were reported, authorities said.

The quake, measuring 5.4 on the Richter scale, struck at 12:54 p.m. (1754 GMT) and was centred in a mountainous area southwest of Bucaramanga, capital of northern Santander province, spokesmen for the National Seismological Institute said.

It was felt across much of northern Colombia, and was powerful enough to inflict serious damage. But it occurred at least 90 miles (150 km) beneath the Earth's surface, so its potential for destruction was curbed, they said.
